fy.label: FY
fy.def: A company's fiscal year; Oracle's FY27 runs June 2026 to May 2027, so its quarters do not match the calendar.

capex.label: Capex
capex.def: Capital expenditure: what a company spends on buildings, chips and equipment rather than on running costs. For a cloud company, mostly data centers and GPUs.

guidance.label: Guidance
guidance.def: The company's own forecast for the coming quarter or year, given with its results. "Raised" or "cut" guidance moves stocks more than the results themselves.

rpo.label: RPO
rpo.def: Remaining performance obligations: contracts customers have signed that the company has not yet delivered or billed. The order book.

bookings.label: Bookings
bookings.def: New orders received in the quarter, as opposed to revenue, which is what was delivered. Bookings say what next year looks like.

backlog.label: Backlog
backlog.def: Orders received but not yet delivered. A growing backlog means demand is outrunning capacity.

lead_time.label: Lead time
lead_time.def: How long a customer waits between ordering and receiving. Lengthening lead times are the clearest sign of a bottleneck.

operating_profit.label: Operating profit
operating_profit.def: Profit from the core business before interest and tax; margin is that profit as a share of revenue. A rising margin means pricing power.

sequentially.label: Sequentially
sequentially.def: Compared with the previous quarter, not with the same quarter last year. The faster signal.

h2.label: H2
h2.def: The second half of the fiscal year.

consensus.label: Consensus
consensus.def: The average of analysts' forecasts. "Above consensus" means the company beat what the market expected.

preliminary_numbers.label: Preliminary numbers
preliminary_numbers.def: Samsung publishes rough quarterly figures about three weeks before the full report. The first hard signal of the quarter.

customer_mix.label: Customer mix
customer_mix.def: Which customers make up a supplier's revenue, and in what order. A change in the order is a change in who is building.

anchor_customer.label: Anchor customer
anchor_customer.def: The first big customer who commits to a new plant, making the rest of the investment safe.

second_source.label: Second source
second_source.def: A second supplier for the same part, kept so no single supplier can hold the customer. Most of this map has none.

wafer.label: Wafer
wafer.def: The round silicon disc chips are built on; 300mm is the standard size. Wafer shipments are the rawest measure of how busy the fabs are.

msi.label: MSI
msi.def: Millions of square inches: the industry's quarterly count of silicon wafer area shipped worldwide.

fab.label: Fab
fab.def: A chip factory. Building one takes two to three years and tens of billions of dollars.

foundry.label: Foundry
foundry.def: A company that manufactures chips designed by others. TSMC is the largest; "a US foundry alternative" means someone else who can do it.

process_node.label: Process node
process_node.def: A generation of chip manufacturing; smaller numbers are newer and denser. 2nm and A14 (TSMC) and 14A (Intel) are the next ones.

yield.label: Yield
yield.def: The share of chips on a wafer that work. Low yield on a new process is why a foundry loses money on it at first.

wfe.label: WFE
wfe.def: Wafer-fab equipment: the machines inside a fab. WFE spending is the health check of the whole equipment layer.

euv.label: EUV
euv.def: Extreme-ultraviolet lithography: the light used to print the smallest chip features. ASML is the only maker of the machines.

high_na.label: High-NA
high_na.def: The next generation of EUV machines, larger optics for even finer printing. A count of units is a count of who is building the next node.

photoresist.label: Photoresist
photoresist.def: The light-sensitive coating that EUV prints into. Three Japanese companies make almost all of it; "dry resist" is a new kind that would change who controls it.

coater.label: Coater
coater.def: The machine that applies resist to a wafer before EUV printing. Tokyo Electron is the sole supplier for EUV.

mask.label: Mask
mask.def: The stencil EUV prints from; the blank is the polished plate it is made on. Two companies in the world make EUV blanks; one company can inspect the finished mask.

advanced_packaging.label: Advanced packaging
advanced_packaging.def: Stacking a GPU and its memory on one base inside the package. CoWoS is TSMC's version, and every AI accelerator passes through it.

osat.label: OSAT
osat.def: Outsourced assembly and test: companies that package and test chips for others. ASE and Amkor are the largest.

substrate.label: Substrate
substrate.def: The board a chip sits on inside its package. ABF is the insulating film in almost all of them (one maker: Ajinomoto); glass is the candidate to replace it.

hbm.label: HBM
hbm.def: High-bandwidth memory: stacks of memory chips bonded next to the GPU. HBM4 is the next generation; whoever supplies NVIDIA's HBM holds the memory chokepoint.

tc_bonder.label: TC bonder
tc_bonder.def: The machine that stacks HBM layers with heat and pressure. Hanmi and ASMPT are the two makers.

base_die.label: Base die
base_die.def: The bottom logic chip in an HBM4 stack, now made at TSMC rather than by the memory maker — which is why margins are in question.

soc_test.label: SoC test
soc_test.def: Testing finished chips on automated test equipment. Advantest tests about two of every three advanced chips.

blackwell.label: Blackwell
blackwell.def: NVIDIA's current and next GPU generations. "Rubin on schedule" is the question every supplier's 2027 depends on.

trainium.label: Trainium
trainium.def: Amazon's in-house AI chip, its alternative to buying from NVIDIA.

datacenter_revenue.label: Datacenter revenue
datacenter_revenue.def: The part of a supplier's sales that goes into AI servers, reported separately so investors can see the AI line.

transceiver.label: Transceiver
transceiver.def: The optical module that links servers with light; 1.6T is the next speed. Coherent is the largest Western maker.

inp_indium_phosphide.label: InP (indium phosphide)
inp_indium_phosphide.def: The material inside the lasers of every fast optical link. Almost all of the substrate is made in China; the export license is the chokepoint.

germanium.label: Germanium
germanium.def: Metals inside optics and power chips; China supplies most of the world's and has used export bans as leverage.

rare_earth_magnets.label: Rare-earth magnets
rare_earth_magnets.def: Magnets in every motor, drive and actuator; China controls the supply and can require licenses to export them.

export_license.label: Export license
export_license.def: Government permission to ship a restricted material or tool abroad. When licenses stop, the supply stops.

goes_electrical_steel.label: GOES (electrical steel)
goes_electrical_steel.def: Grain-oriented electrical steel: the special steel inside power transformers. One US plant makes it.

lpt_large_power_transformer.label: LPT (large power transformer)
lpt_large_power_transformer.def: The transformer that connects a data center to the grid. Lead times are currently around three years.

gas_turbine.label: Gas turbine
gas_turbine.def: Turbines that generate power on site for data centers; "slots" are the delivery positions in the maker's queue, now reserved years ahead. IGT = industrial gas turbine.

blade_castings.label: Blade castings
blade_castings.def: The cast metal blades inside a gas turbine. Two companies can make them; the queue is 60–90 weeks.

spie.label: SPIE
spie.def: The annual lithography conference where TSMC, Intel and the equipment makers publish their next-generation results.
